capabilities: scan the vault for attachment files not referenced by Markdown notes or Canvas files
respect Obsidian's configured attachment folder and accept manual folder input
review unused candidates in a modal with search, extension filters, sorting and bulk selection
generate a preview-only report and show quick previews before deletion
move selected files to trash and safe-list known files from future scans
extras: Much of the described behavior is planned or at the first-milestone stage rather than fully shipped; the project began as a legacy Python script that is no longer part of the plugin runtime; desktop-only release target; no account, telemetry, ads or paid service.
motivation: The author originally wrote a Python prototype and reshaped it as a plugin because a plugin works directly on the opened vault, needs no manual path entry, and can delete files respecting Obsidian's trash behavior.
problem: Deleting notes leaves attachment files orphaned in the vault, and Obsidian has no built-in way to find which attachments are no longer referenced.
summary: Unused attachment cleaner that scans the vault for attachment files no longer referenced by notes or Canvas files and lets you trash them after review.
